_doc: WireGuard PUBLIC mesh endpoint declarations for the Surface Pro NixOS host. Mirrors the schema of wireguard-endpoints.json, but for the wg-public interface (10.1.0.0/24 mesh on udp/51821, hub = oci-analytics). Source of truth lives in cloud/config.json#native.wireguard_public + the per-VM publickeys in vault/A0_keys/providers/wireguard/<vm>-public/. Replicated verbatim here because Nix pure-eval flakes cannot read paths outside their own source root. Regenerate by running `bash ~/git/cloud/2_configs/build.sh all` then copying the relevant slice of dist/_cloud-data-consolidated.json. Phase 1 of the wg-public client extension (zany-popping plan) — Surface + Termux added as client peers in addition to wg0.
_ipv6_doc: wg-public dual-stack fields (2026-07-26). Verified in cloud/a_solutions/infra-net_wireguard-public/build.json (wireguard_public.subnet_v6 = fd0c:1d01::/64; peers/clients each carry wg_ipv6, including surface = fd0c:1d01::5, hub oci-analytics = fd0c:1d01::1). client.wg_ipv6/subnet_v6 mirror that data so this host's NM profile can add ipv6.method=manual instead of ignore.
_tunnel_mode_doc: split | full. split = only subnet + subnet_v6 are routed into the tunnel (mesh-only; the rest of your traffic uses the local WiFi/LTE). full = 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0 are routed into the tunnel (all traffic exits via the hub). Read by configuration_network.nix, which derives BOTH the peer allowed-ips AND ipv4/ipv6.never-default AND the dispatcher-script wg set from this one field — never edit those three by hand or they will disagree. Only ONE interface may be full at a time: two default routes over two wg devices fight.
